thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 inference latency spike detected in eu-prod dedicated pool (p99 > 1200ms) — routing impacted. Auto-scale attempted and failed. page: oncall-uk
oncall-uk: Acked. I'm paged and jumping in. Starting triage: checking pool health and recent deploys.
maria_s: I'm looking at runtime logs for shard-eu-2, seeing lots of kernel timeouts and OOM-ish churn around 16:12 UTC.
ajay_r: I'm on model routing. Noticing degraded backpressure — queue length up 6x for requests to gpt-like-xxl-quant.
kyle_eng: I can run a soft rollback to the previous kernel build on shard-eu-2 if we want a quick mitigation. Will need ~5m to rollout.
nate_sre: Before rolling, let's check if we can hot-route traffic to compatible variant (gpt-like-xxl-8bit) to reduce memory pressure. That might avoid churn.
emily_acc: Heads-up: two enterprise customers (AcmeHealth, DataFlow) reported elevated latencies via support. Need a customer-facing status ASAP.
oncall-uk: Agreed. Immediate steps: 1) hot-route 20% traffic away from shard-eu-2 to eu-fallback via routing policy, 2) scale dedicated pool by +2 instances (manual), 3) prepare rollback if no improvement in 5m. Executing step 1 now.
ops-bot: action: routing.update policy=hot-route percentage=20 target=eu-fallback details="route 20% traffic from shard-eu-2 to eu-fallback"
maria_s: Routing change accepted, queues on shard-eu-2 show small drop, cpu still high. Initiating step 2: scaling pool.
ajay_r: While scaling, I see repeated kernel panic logs: 
```
[2026-03-16T16:12:05Z] kernel-infer: kernel_select failed: cuLaunchKernel returned CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_OUT_OF_RESOURCES
[2026-03-16T16:12:06Z] evicting KV cache for session 0x7f9b
```
kyle_eng: Those look like a regression in the 1.4.3 kernel we rolled out yesterday. I'm going to trigger rollback on shard-eu-2 now. Command: `rwdctl deploy rollback --shard shard-eu-2 --to-tag kernel-1.4.2`
oncall-uk: Proceed. Noting customer impact and timeline for status update.
ops-bot: action: deploy.rollback shard=shard-eu-2 to=kernel-1.4.2 status=started
maria_s: Scaling completed (+2 instances). CPU on fallback nodes moderate. Rollback in progress.
kyle_eng: Rollback finished on shard-eu-2, restarting runtime processes. Watching metrics.
ajay_r: p99 dropped from ~1.35s to ~0.9s across the pool after rollback and routing. Good sign.
emily_acc: Preparing customer notification now. Proposed short template: 
"We detected elevated API latencies in our EU inference pool affecting a subset of requests. We’ve routed traffic to fallback capacity and rolled back a recent runtime kernel. We expect normal performance to resume shortly. We’ll update here in 30 minutes and follow up with a full incident report"
oncall-uk: Solid. I'm posting a status page update now. Status content: 
"Investigating — Increased latency for EU inference: We are investigating an elevation in p99 latency for inference requests in the eu-prod dedicated pool. Mitigations in progress: traffic routing, capacity increase, runtime rollback. Customer impact: intermittent higher latencies for some requests. ETA for recovery: 15–30 minutes. More details at /incidents/1769005000."
ops-bot: action: statuspage.update incident=1769005000 state=investigating impact=partial region=eu details_url="https://status.redwood.com/incidents/1769005000"
maria_s: Watching internal metrics — tail latencies still noisy but trending down. No error-rate increase beyond normal.
nate_sre: Good. For the handoff at 16:35 UTC, if still unresolved, assign postmortem to kyle_eng and set Sev level to P1 until full recovery.
oncall-uk: Noted. Current timeline: 16:12 page triggered -> 16:15 routing -> 16:18 scale -> 16:22 rollback -> 16:28 partial recovery observed. Will keep monitoring.
emily_acc: I'm sending targeted notices to AcmeHealth and DataFlow with the template and mention of mitigation actions.
kyle_eng: Quick signal: `kubectl top` shows GPU memory pressure dropped ~30% on shard-eu-2 after rollback. No further OOM logs.
ajay_r: Throughput recovering to baseline. We should monitor for 2x normal window before fully closing.
nate_sre: If traffic stabilizes for 30 minutes, we can de-escalate to P2 and hand back to engineering for postmortem.
oncall-uk: I'll create the internal post-incident channel and tag owners. Postmortem owners: kyle_eng (runtime), maria_s (observability), ajay_r (routing). Target initial draft in 48h.
emily_acc: Customer follow-up templates (short & detailed) added to the internal doc: 
Short: "We experienced intermittent elevated latencies in the EU inference pool. Mitigations were applied and service performance has returned to expected levels. A detailed post-incident summary will be provided."
Detailed: "Summary: On 2026-03-16 16:12 UTC we observed elevated p99 inference latency in eu-prod dedicated pool caused by a regression in kernel-1.4.3 leading to memory launch failures. Impact: intermittent latency increases for a subset of requests. Mitigation: hot-routing, scale-up, rollback to kernel-1.4.2. Recovery: performance returned to normal after rollback and routing adjustments. Next steps: revert kernel rollout plan, add pre-deploy memory stress tests, and update alert thresholds."
oncall-uk: Current status: monitoring; p99 ~880ms and stable for 6 minutes. Posting updated status page entry now: state=identified -> "Mitigations applied; routing and rollback performed. Service performance improving; monitoring in progress. ETA to full recovery: 10–20 minutes."
ops-bot: action: statuspage.update incident=1769005000 state=identified impact=partial update="Mitigations applied; monitoring in progress."
maria_s: Leaving logs + grep snippet for follow-up: 
```
# count kernel panic events in last hour
zcat /var/log/rwd/runtime.log.*.gz | grep -c "kernel_select failed"
```
josh: (watching, not in channel earlier) Suggest we add a synthetic test to run against eu-fallback for 1h to ensure no regressions.
noncall-uk: Good call. Adding synthetic monitor run for 1h.
emily_acc: Sent customer messages. AcmeHealth confirms reduced latency on their side. DataFlow acknowledges and asks for RCA timeline.
kyle_eng: I recommend we block kernel-1.4.3 from further rollouts until we have regression test coverage. Will open a PR for the rollout guard.
ate_sre: Agreed. Also propose adding a metric for kernel launch failures to trigger earlier alerts.
oncall-uk: Handoff plan: if stable for next 20m, I'll hand back to on-call rotation for monitoring and set follow-up tasks. Otherwise keep paging.
emily_acc: I'll coordinate account outreach and prep a CSM briefing doc.
ops-bot: action: monitor.synthetic start target=eu-fallback duration=3600 status=running
maria_s: p99 stable at 820ms for 12 minutes, error rates normal.
oncall-uk: We're moving towards de-escalation. Final status update in 15m, then handback. Great work team. :tada:
